title: SAFE-CARE: A Framework for Designing and Evaluating Safe Healthcare AI Agents
description:
SAFE-CARE™ is an open framework for designing, evaluating and releasing patient-facing healthcare AI agents. This record archives version 1.3.0 of its public repository: the framework text, eleven companion documents, six machine-readable templates, four example scenarios and a repeat-run tool, all built to drop into an engineering workflow.

What is new in 1.3.0

Version 1.3.0 adds the step that comes before every release gate: qualifying the evaluation instrument. Because an unchanged agent does not give the same answers twice, a single benchmark run cannot tell a real change from noise. To close that gap, the release adds instrument qualification (repeat runs, a noise floor, judge calibration against a clinician band, judged-turn coverage and a positive control for every hard-fail gate) and change control that scales re-testing to the type of change. On top of that, release gates are now read on repeat runs and one-sided lower bounds, the judge rubric treats safety as a gate before any score, and the scenario schema moves to version 1.1. White paper v2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.23826804) reports what the first published SAFE-CARE Bench run found.

What is in the deposit

The framework document sets out the full method, from use-case scoping through production monitoring. Around it sit eleven companion documents: a one-page overview, a risk taxonomy of ten failure modes with their required controls, an anonymized menopause-support case study, the A0 to A4 ablation template, the scenario simulation schema, the AI judge rubric, the release gate checklist, the safety case template, a conference talk outline, instrument qualification and change control. Each also ships as a branded DOCX and PDF.

Machine-readable artifacts

Six templates are released under Apache-2.0 for direct reuse: the use-case safety card, the scenario schema, the AI judge rubric, the release gate checklist, the instrument qualification record and the change control map. Four synthetic example scenarios cover a critical red flag, a medication boundary, a case that needs clarification and a case that needs no escalation. In addition, a standard-library Python tool, with tests, computes the noise floor, the smallest detectable difference, one-sided lower bounds and the minimum scenario library a gate needs.

How to use it

A team building a patient-facing AI agent can adopt this repository as a working governance baseline. In practice, the team completes the use-case safety card before choosing a model, grounds every health claim in approved evidence, encodes scenarios against the schema, qualifies its evaluation instrument, and gates each release on the checklist. A 30-day implementation path is included for teams starting from a narrow education use case.

Public-release boundary

This deposit discloses reusable methodology only. It contains no proprietary prompts, client implementation details, source-library contents, real user data, private datasets, screenshots, credentials or deployment protocols, and the applied case study is anonymized.

Standards alignment

WHO AI-for-health guidance (2021) and large multi-modal model guidance (2024); NIST AI Risk Management Framework; NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile; FDA Software-as-a-Medical-Device and Good Machine Learning Practice; FTC Health Breach Notification Rule. The EU AI Act and ONC HTI-1 are tracked for applicability.
